question.text: Under SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations 2003, 'fraud' in connection with securities includes which of the following?

answer.text: Only wilful misstatement that causes financial loss to the counterparty
Only insider trading under a separate insider-trading regulation
Only acts by registered intermediaries, not by issuers themselves
Any act, expression, omission or concealment to induce another person to deal in securities — with or without wrongful gain or loss

explanation.text: The Logic: Under PFUTP 2003, fraud is defined inclusively as any act, expression, omission or concealment committed to induce another person (or his agent) to deal in securities. The definition expressly does not require wrongful gain or loss as a necessary element, so reckless misrepresentations and concealment of material fact can be in scope. The Trap: Option A is too narrow because it requires loss. Option B confuses PFUTP with the separate Prohibition of Insider Trading regulations. Option C is wrong because PFUTP applies to issuers and intermediaries alike rather than only to one of them. Note: An AIR with reckless wording — for example, headline beneficiary numbers without sampled evidence — can fall within this inclusive definition if it is capable of inducing dealings in the listed instrument.
